feat(typography): adopt the new Canonical type scale

Update heading font sizes to the Canonical type-scale spec and replace the
hand-tuned baseline nudges with values generated from real font metrics by
@lyubomir-popov/baseline-nudge-generator.

- display 5rem -> 5.25rem (84px) with line-height 11 -> 12 baseline units;
  80px was not a step on the scale, 84px is one octave above h1
- h1/h2 2.5rem -> 2.625rem (42px); mobile stays 2rem
- every nudge regenerated, collapsed into shared variables per size pair
- h1/h2 take one extra baseline unit on the nudge, so a 42px cap is not closer
  to preceding content than body text is

Spacing is untouched: sp-after and sp-before keep their existing values, so the
p + heading pair rules behave exactly as before. Every level still occupies a
whole number of baseline units.

Mean absolute first-baseline error against the grid is 0.526px, against
0.535px for the previous hand-tuned values.

Adds a multi-line rhythm audit to the typographic-spacing example and tests
covering the generated values and the whole-unit invariant.
